added_failures_note: derived from the reviewed manifest's after_suite gate log (logs/gate-head-final.log, revision 58e739298a3e374517e581dc078281cec4c28ff7, EXIT=0, failure_ids []): the head arm holds no failure, so no failure can be added against any base and the count is 0. The reviewed manifest records no baseline_suite, so no baseline id list existed either way; this 0 is a property of the empty head arm, not a base-to-head diff. The two added failures the gate arm does not cover (tests/test_served_code_drift.py) are named as findings below.

reckon/serve.py:3459 Handler.do_GET /_checks/<project> and :3468 _start_refresh as the pending-document trigger

findings.text: blocking: renaming _CHECK_REFRESH_ENABLED to _REFRESH_ENABLED in reckon/serve.py:1030 leaves two tests in this file failing at head that passed at base - the assertions at :301, :307 and :482 read the old attribute - so the landed change adds two failures to a suite that imports reckon/serve.py, and the source done_when requires such suites to show no added failure against base; logs/out-of-scope-drift.log records 2 failed, 24 passed, EXIT=1. The file is outside the node's granted write paths, so the repair is the one-word name on those three lines, owed to whoever owns the file, not a duplicate of the node's own work.

follow-on: the source manifest's orientation_base_sha is 4233bbcaf16613d1421b0731ecef4273f7f4c4ba, which does not resolve in this repository; the parent of the first landed commit 26e8645983c46ca99cbacc13ccedbdf7a4a865f2 is 4233bbcaf2dc7858dda0194b8626cb012439162a. A reader matching the recorded base pair against this review's reviewed_base_sha would find a sha that names no object.

follow-on: the wider serve-importing population arm (131 files) ended EXIT=124 at 98% with roughly fifteen failures showing and no pytest summary line, so the failure identities are unread and the done_when's 'tests importing reckon/serve.py show no added failure against base' is not established for that population; the node's six named suites and the new one pass in full, but the wider clause has no completed arm.

item_verdicts.call_sites: Seven production call sites reach the change: Handler.do_GET at reckon/serve.py:3146, :3459 and :3516, Handler._send_project_changes at :2898/:2928, _FleetChangeWatch._spawn_changes at reckon/change_streams.py:374, the child entry point at reckon/serve.py:4235, and the SPA listener at docs/ui/state-loader.js:737; the node's own test files are excluded.
item_verdicts.diff: Read commit by commit from 4233bbcaf2dc7858dda0194b8626cb012439162a to 58e739298a3e374517e581dc078281cec4c28ff7; 26e86459 generalises the checks refresh into a keyed stored-result mechanism and adds the fleet-event path, and 58e73929 records the landing fragment, all inside the declared scope.
item_verdicts.done_when: The done_when asks for a stubbed-delay recompute per route with a 50 ms answer bound, a marker the stub writes, a one-rollup-child case, a fleet-event case through the parent waiter, and no added failure in serve-importing suites; the gate log records 52 passed EXIT=0 and negative-control.log records EXIT=1 with the three routes at 350.8-351.8 ms against the 50 ms bound, but the serve-importing population clause is unmet.
item_verdicts.goal: The node goal is to serve discovery, the checks summary and the fleet rollup from stored results kept current by one generic child refresh, publishing each fleet-scoped result as a fleet event on every open stream; all three routes now read a store through reckon/serve.py:2393 _served_result and the watch publishes fleet versions through reckon/change_streams.py:340 publish_fleet, with velocity correctly deferred as a later node.
item_verdicts.manifest: The source manifest records status complete, the two commits, a 52-passed EXIT=0 gate at logs/gate-head-final.log, the declared negative control at logs/negative-control.log, the ruff delta, and the tests/test_served_code_drift.py drift as a follow-on; its after_suite arm is readable and its baseline_suite is absent.
item_verdicts.write_paths: The node was granted eleven files (reckon/serve.py, reckon/change_streams.py, reckon/compliance.py, docs/ui/state-loader.js, and seven test files); git diff 4233bbcaf2dc7858dda0194b8626cb012439162a..58e739298a3e374517e581dc078281cec4c28ff7 changes five of them plus the always-permitted landing fragment, so every changed path is inside the declared scope.

justifications.durability: tests/test_the_slow_routes_answer_from_stored_results.py:167-192 asserts each route answers a store-only marker inside a 50 ms bound while a 350 ms recompute runs, which reddens if a route computes inline, and :283-306's one-rollup-child case reddens under the per-project mutant; the fleet-event case at :330-346 relies on a real child and a 20 s stream wait.
justifications.evidence: logs/gate-head-final.log ends 52 passed EXIT=0 and logs/negative-control.log ends EXIT=1 with the three routes at 350.8-351.8 ms against the 50 ms bound, but the done_when's serve-importing population clause is contradicted by logs/out-of-scope-drift.log (2 failed) and unmeasured by logs/serve-importers-head.log (EXIT=124, no summary).
justifications.fit: reckon/serve.py:2393-2417 follows the existing _send_json/headers idiom it extends at :2840 and the module's mechanism-named helpers, and no added symbol carries a plan, phase or ticket label.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/serve.py:3146, :3459 and :3516 answer the rollup, checks and discovery routes from _served_result with an X-Result-Age header, and reckon/change_streams.py:362 _spawn_changes plus reckon/serve.py:2297 _publish_refresh deliver the fleet event the goal names.
justifications.reuse: reckon/serve.py:2201 reuses metadata_index._persisted_cache_path, the same owner compliance.py:139 already stores its verdicts through, and :2231 uses _store.write_json_atomically; the refresh generalises _start_check_refresh in place rather than adding a parallel mechanism.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff 4233bbcaf2dc7858dda0194b8626cb012439162a..58e739298a3e374517e581dc078281cec4c28ff7 changes only declared paths plus the always-permitted fragment, and the plan retires the compliance-only refresh names, so the rename at reckon/serve.py:1030 is implied by the goal.

notes: The fleet-event case (tests/test_the_slow_routes_answer_from_stored_results.py:330-346) runs the real child and asserts exactly one fleet event naming the rollup key reaches a stream open on the temp project, so the production publish path is exercised end to end. No added assertion compares a value against the same variable the test passed in: the 'prior', 'recomputed' and marker dicts are reachable only through the store, so each reddens when a route stops reading it.
